DECOMPOSE_TASK_TOOL:
First decide: can this EXECUTION TASK finish in this thread, or must it split?
Default to FINISHING in this thread. Most tasks can be completed here with tools. Call decompose_task only when the work is genuinely splittable in a *schedulable* sense: multiple deliverables that benefit from parallel execution, independent retry per subtask, or hard ordering dependencies between phases.
Do NOT call decompose_task just because the task is classified complex or seems large. A single thread with good tool usage is usually more efficient than spawning child threads.
Do NOT call when the task is simple or minimal: finish one clear deliverable here with tools. Do NOT use as a personal checklist — use write_todos for that.
## Auto-generation mode
You may call decompose_task with only the `task` argument and omit `subtasks`. In this mode the FAST model generates subtasks from the evidence you have gathered. This is preferred when you have already grounded the task with ls/glob/grep/read_file — the FAST model will produce grounded subtasks faster than you can enumerate them.
When you provide explicit `subtasks`, the grounding critic still verifies them against the evidence.
## Ground your subtasks in evidence
Do not propose subtasks that cite files or directories you have not confirmed exist. Gather evidence first (ls, glob, grep, or read_file) so that every subtask `full_description` references areas your evidence supports. Proposals citing non-existent paths are rejected and you must re-ground before re-proposing.
## Subtask count limit
There is a hard cap on the number of child subtasks per call (shown in the system prompt as "decompose_task subtask limit"). Stay at or under this cap. If the work needs more subtasks than the cap allows, group related items into fewer broader subtasks. Proposing more than the cap causes the entire proposal to be rejected, cancelling all subtasks.
Args: task, subtasks[{description, full_description, expected_output, execution_hint, depends_on_local, task_complexity}]. Dependencies among the proposed subtasks only: depends_on_local (0-based indexes into this same list). For each subtask, set task_complexity to "simple" (single focused step) or "complex" (needs further decomposition). When subtasks is omitted, the FAST model generates them from gathered evidence.
